HR-deficient cells become sensitive to PARP inhibition and cisplatin.
Genomic instability in mammary epithelium is the proposed route to the ER-negative and triple-negative breast cancers enriched in carriers.
DNA-repair infidelity is proposed by the primary authors as a mechanism contributing to neuroblastoma initiation in carriers.
Reproduces chromosomally unstable triple-negative mammary carcinoma after Bard1 loss.

evidence.reference_title: Germline loss-of-function variants in the BARD1 gene are associated with early-onset familial breast cancer but not ovarian cancer.
evidence.snippet: Due to the significant association of germline LoF variants in BARD1 with early-onset BC, we suggest that intensified BC surveillance programs should be offered to women carrying pathogenic BARD1 gene variants.

nodes.description: Female breast cancer is the established manifestation, at moderate risk. In BCAC (protein-truncating variants) the overall odds ratio in population-based studies was 2.09 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.23), with estimated absolute risk by age 80 in the 17 to 30% moderate-risk range; in the population-based CARRIERS study the overall odds ratio was 1.37 (95% CI 0.87 to 2.16), not significant. Both consortia found stronger associations with estrogen-receptor-negative disease. In familial German index patients, carriers were diagnosed younger (mean 42.3 years) and the association was not significant at age 50 or older.

nodes.description: Common and rare neuroblastoma-associated BARD1 germline variants were associated with lower BARD1 mRNA and higher DNA-damage burden. Bard1-null mouse cells are aneuploid, and mammary-specific Bard1 inactivation produces tumors with high chromosomal instability. HRD has been observed in triple-negative carrier breast tumors with LOH but not in non-triple-negative primaries.

evidence.snippet: This result, together with the increased chromosomal aneuploidy of Bard1 mutant cells, indicates a role for Bard1 in maintaining genomic stability.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline nonsense, frameshift, copy-number and selected missense variants reduce functional BARD1. BARD1 is required for the ubiquitin ligase activity of the BRCA1-BARD1 RING heterodimer; individually, BRCA1 and BARD1 have very low ligase activity in vitro. ClinGen describes the pathogenic mechanism as loss of function with disrupted BRCA1 binding and loss of DNA damage response. In isogenic neuroblastoma and RPE1 cells, single-allele truncating variants were sufficient to reduce repair efficiency (haploinsufficiency).

evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is loss of function in which BRCA1 binding is disrupted and subsequent loss of DNA damage response.

evidence.reference_title: The RING heterodimer BRCA1-BARD1 is a ubiquitin ligase inactivated by a breast cancer-derived mutation.
evidence.snippet: Whereas individually BRCA1 and BARD1 have very low ubiquitin ligase activities in vitro, BRCA1 combined with BARD1 exhibits dramatically higher activity.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a RING protein that can interact in vivo with the BRCA1 gene product.
evidence.snippet: The BARD1/BRCA1 interaction is disrupted by BRCA1 missense mutations that segregate with breast cancer susceptibility, indicating that BARD1 may be involved in mediating tumour suppression by BRCA1.

nodes.description: BRCA1-BARD1 binds DNA and RAD51 and stimulates RAD51-mediated synaptic-complex assembly during homologous recombination. BARD1 variants that are non-functional in homology-directed-repair reporter assays sensitize cells to ionizing radiation and cisplatin, and this assay separates known pathogenic from known benign BARD1 variants.

evidence.reference_title: Functional analysis of BARD1 missense variants in homology-directed repair and damage sensitivity.
evidence.snippet: Two known benign variants were found to be functional in HDR, and three known pathogenic variants were non-functional, supporting the notion that the HDR assay can be used to predict the clinical risk of BARD1 variants.

nodes.description: Mammary-specific Bard1 inactivation produced carcinomas indistinguishable from conditional Brca1 and double-mutant tumors in frequency, latency, histopathology and cytogenetics. The tumors were triple-negative and basal-like. The model is biallelic and tissue-restricted, not a heterozygous germline model.

evidence.reference_title: The basal-like mammary carcinomas induced by Brca1 or Bard1 inactivation implicate the BRCA1/BARD1 heterodimer in tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: Significantly, the conditional Bard1- and Brca1-mutant mice developed breast carcinomas that are indistinguishable from each other (and from those of double conditional Bard1/Brca1-mutant animals) with respect to their frequency, latency, histopathology, and cytogenetic features.

nodes.description: Rare germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic BARD1 variants were the most significantly enriched cancer-predisposition-gene finding among 786 neuroblastoma patients, and rare germline copy-number variants disrupting BARD1 were found in patients but not in cancer-free controls. A pediatric pan-cancer germline analysis also found the BARD1-neuroblastoma association (6 of 485 neuroblastoma cases). Absolute penetrance in carriers is not reported in these sources. The one case report used here describes metastatic high-risk neuroblastoma diagnosed at 22 months.

nodes.description: Loss of the wild-type BARD1 allele is documented in a subset of carrier tumors but has not been shown to be universal. In a French case-control study, two of seven interpretable carrier breast tumors (both triple-negative primaries) showed loss of heterozygosity with an HRD phenotype, a metastasis showed LOH without HRD, and non-triple-negative primaries had neither. In a child with a germline BARD1 frameshift and refractory neuroblastoma, mono-allelic expression of the variant and loss of BARD1 protein on immunohistochemistry indicated biallelic loss in the tumor.

evidence.reference_title: BARD1 and breast cancer genetic predisposition: case-control study and HRD signature analysis.
evidence.snippet: Among these, two triple-negative (TN) primary tumors exhibited both biallelic BARD1 inactivation via loss of heterozygosity (LOH) and an HRD phenotype; one metastasis displayed LOH without HRD. All non-TN primary tumors lacked both biallelic inactivation and HRD.

nodes.description: One child with a germline BARD1 frameshift, somatic BARD1 protein loss and refractory high-risk neuroblastoma had a complete bone-marrow response to talazoparib plus irinotecan and remained without clinical evidence of disease 32 months off therapy. This is a single case report plus preclinical data, not an established indication.
